movesets.name: Defog
movesets.description: 88 Speed EVs let Talonflame outspeed Landorus-T.

strategies.overview: Talonflame is a fantastic support Pokemon that can utilize its high Speed and access to recovery to serve as a reliable pivot and Defogger. Flame Body and Will-O-Wisp, combined with a resistance to common attacks like U-turn and Close Combat, allow Talonflame to deter and punish attacks from pivots like Mienshao and Galarian Zapdos as well as cripple physical setup sweepers like Maushold and Bisharp. Talonflame is also able to switch into and make progress on relatively passive defensive Pokemon like non-Stone Edge Hippowdon, Chesnaught, and Registeel, especially if it carries Taunt to prevent recovery. Unfortunately, Talonflame's lack of firepower and special bulk can give special attackers like Hisuian Goodra, Armarouge, and Slowbro a free turn to fire off an attack or set up after switching in safely, though the latter can be mitigated by Taunt. Furthermore, Talonflame's 4x weakness to Stealth Rock can pose a problem, as many attackers that it would like to switch in on, like Krookodile and Galarian Zapdos, carry Knock Off, which can remove Heavy-Duty Boots and cripple Talonflame's ability to pivot if Stealth Rock is set up.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Flare Blitz is an alternative over Brave Bird that hits Steel-types like Jirachi and Magnezone, though it weakens Talonflame's matchup against common Pokemon like Cyclizar, Slowbro, and Noivern. Swords Dance is an option to turn Talonflame into a wincon that can utilize its Speed to clean up a chipped opposition late-game.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Specially offensive Steel-types like Empoleon, Magnezone, and Hisuian Goodra take little damage from Brave Bird and threaten Talonflame back with strong attacks. Talonflame is similarly unable to do anything to Jirachi, which can choose to risk a burn in order to make progress via Body Slam, Stealth Rock, or Wish.

Water-types: Water-types like Slowbro, Basculegion-F, and Volcanion are able to easily OHKO Talonflame.

Special Wallbreakers: Many special wallbreakers that don't fall into the aforementioned types, such as Armarouge, Reuniclus, and Raikou, also take little damage from Talonflame's Brave Bird and can use it as an opportunity to fire off attacks or set up.

Rock-type Attacks: Rock-type Pokemon like Rhyperior, Lycanroc-D, and Terrakion threaten Talonflame with an OHKO. Similarly, Hippowdon and Krookodile can run Rock-type coverage in Stone Edge to eliminate Talonflame. While all of these Pokemon can be crippled by Will-O-Wisp, they can still OHKO or deal significant damage to Talonflame.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description:
Set Details

Will-O-Wisp gives Talonflame a more reliable way of crippling physical attackers like Mimikyu, Krookodile, and Bisharp. Taunt prevents defensive Pokemon like Hippowdon and Gastrodon and setup sweepers like Armarouge and Reuniclus from taking advantage of Talonflame's passivity by safely setting up entry hazards, healing up, or boosting their stats. U-turn allows Talonflame to pivot out to offensive threats like Armarouge, Gardevoir, and Mienshao that can exploit its switch-ins like Hippowdon, Slowbro, and Hisuian Goodra. Defog pairs well with Talonflame's ability to force out physical attackers and access to recovery. Roost is important recovery, though Talonflame should be wary of Earthquake from Hippowdon and Krookodile when using it. Heavy-Duty Boots is necessary to allow Talonflame to switch in while Stealth Rock is up. Flame Body is useful for punishing Pokemon like Maushold, Maushold, and Cyclizar. Tera Ground gives Talonflame an immunity to Electric-type attacks from Magnezone and Raikou. Tera Water provides a valuable resistance to Water-type attacks from Barraskewda, Basculegion-F, and Volcanion. Tera Fairy retains Talonflame's important resistances to Bug- and Fighting-type attacks from pivots like Galarian Zapdos and Mienshao while allowing it to absorb a Draco Meteor from Cyclizar, Hisuian Goodra, or Noivern and shrug off Knock Off from Krookodile. All of these options additionally assist Talonflame by removing its glaring Stealth Rock weakness for if Heavy-Duty Boots is removed.

Talonflame fits best on offense and balance structures as a pivot and deterrent against physical attacks thanks to Flame Body. Its typing pairs well with specially defensive Pokemon like Umbreon, Wo-Chien, and Hisuian Goodra that fear attacks from Fighting-type wallbreakers like Galarian Zapdos and Gallade. Talonflame's high Speed and access to recovery can provide great value particularly to bulky structures like stall teams, as it can neutralize strong attackers and setup sweepers like Maushold, Bisharp, and niche picks such as Gallade that may be difficult to deal with otherwise. On more offensive structures, U-turn can allow wallbreakers like Armarouge, Hisuian Goodra, and Crawdaunt to safely switch into and threaten Talonflame's defensive checks like Hippowdon and Slowbro. Talonflame's reliability as a fast Defogger is also appreciated by partners such as Galarian Zapdos, Choice Band Entei, and non-Heavy-Duty Boots Gyarados that are vulnerable to entry hazard chip damage.

movesets.name: Defog (Fire)
movesets.description:
Talonflame, due to its Ground immunity and access to entry hazard removal with Defog, has a great spot on Fire teams. Gale Wings makes Brave Bird a priority move at full HP, which allows Talonflame to take out threats like Ogerpon-W, Choice Scarf Great Tusk, and Keldeo. Will-O-Wisp weakens physical threats like Mamoswine, Garchomp, Iron Treads, and Excadrill; U-turn can be run over Will-O-Wisp to let Talonflame hit Meowscarada and Hoopa-U while also allowing it to pivot into one of its teammates. But doing so will remove the opportunity to weaken the aforementioned physical threats with a burn, which can be a problem for the team. Heavy-Duty Boots is the go-to item that lets Talonflame avoid taking damage from Stealth Rock. The given EV spread lets Talonflame outspeed and OHKO Ogerpon-W with Brave Bird.

All of Talonflame's teammates appreciate the removal of hazards and Ground immunity that Talonflame provides. Swords Dance Ogerpon-H is an amazing teammate for Talonflame, taking out pesky Water- and Rock-types like Primarina, Quagsire, and Rhyperior at +2 with Horn Leech. Swords Dance Ceruledge is a great setup sweeper that can deal with pesky Psychic- and Ghost-types like Iron Boulder and Flutter Mane with Shadow Sneak after a boost. Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine is a great wallbreaker for Talonflame, being able to take out Flying-types like Gyarados, Dragonite, and Skarmory. Volcanion provides a Water immunity for Talonflame while checking Azumarill with Sludge Wave. Heatran tanks special hits from the likes of Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Power Gem while OHKOing it back with Heavy Slam. Heatran also traps walls like Toxapex with Magma Storm and stops them from recovering with Taunt.

strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Talonflame is most common as the main supportive option on teams that aim to overwhelm the opponent and win quickly, such as hyper offense, where priority speed control in the form of Tailwind is especially valuable. Its most common partner by far is Choice Specs Gholdengo, which, when paired with Covert Cloak Talonflame, prevents Fake Out and makes it difficult to stop a turn one Tailwind + Tera Steel Make it Rain. This duo is also particularly strong with Dondozo and Commander Tatsugiri, softening up teams for Dondozo to clean up in the endgame.
  • Talonflame doesn't particularly need any partners to function well; it instead serves to complement its teammates.
  • Talonflame's main competition is Whimsicott, which doesn't have to worry about about losing access to priority moves thanks to Prankster, as well as having better enabling tools such as Sunny Day for Hisuian Typhlosion and Delphox and Beat Up for Annihilape. Talonflame has more general utility tools with Will-O-Wisp and non-Prankster Taunt, is faster, and can OHKO it first with priority Brave Bird, but it generally isn't as support-oriented as Whimsicott.

Strategy Comments

  • Talonflame's biggest strength is immediate turn one pressure. Take advantage of that. You generally always want to be leading Talonflame and setting up Tailwind; going for an attack is risky before Tailwind is up, as you lose Gale Wings and a significant chunk of Talonflame's health. Once Tailwind is up, sacrificing it for a free switch is usually the play. If you have the opportunity for a safe switch, however, take it, as Talonflame's coverage and Speed makes it a great late-game cleaner.
  • The only real reason to use Talonflame over Whimsicott is coverage and damage, functioning almost like a glass cannon with access to priority Tailwind. Flying- and Fire-type coverage is excellent into the metagame, and its Speed means it's always a credible threat. Go for damage whenever possible after setting up Tailwind.
  • The best way to handle Talonflame is to nullify either its damage or priority speed control. Pokemon with Intimidate severely hamper Talonflame's offensive pressure, and even Pokemon like Electabuzz and Primarina that can eat one of its attacks and return back for strong damage are difficult matchups. Alternatively, nullifying its priority or Speed advantage also works well. Priority attacks like Fake Out and Extreme Speed break Gale Wings, with the former often completely preventing Tailwind from being set up on non-Covert Cloak sets. Priority blocking abilities like both Indeedee's Psychic Surge are difficult but not common. Incineroar is likely the biggest pain spot for Talonflame teams, as it walls Gholdengo, can break Gale Wings with Fake Out, and has Intimidate to cripple Talonflame offensively. If you're playing Talonflame, you have to be careful when leading it into Incineroar and Sneasler teams, and usually, it's best to completely leave it behind in matchups against balance teams.

movesets.name: Offensive Tailwind Support
movesets.description:
• Talonflame takes over for Tornadus as the premier offensive Tailwind support, dealing huge damage with its primary STAB attacks that give it immediate offensive pressure as well as having a host of supportive options with Gale Wings Tailwind.
  • Covert Cloak is the most popular item on Talonflame, preventing opposing Fake Outs from slowing down a offensive lead. Talonflame's high Speed means it's usually not too bothered by Gale Wings breaking. Life Orb and Sharp Beak are two sides of the same coin; they are offensive items to pick up OHKOes on foes that Covert Cloak sets don't at the cost of being vulnerable to Fake Out. Life Orb allows for cleaner OHKOes such as OHKOing Rillaboom regardless of its defensive investment as well as boosting Flare Blitz, while Sharp Beak is an option if you prefer not taking recoil at the cost of damage output, such as only having a 60% chance to OHKO the previously mentioned Rillaboom.
  • The choice of Tera type is mostly dependent on personal preference. Tera Ghost prevents Fake Out, Extreme Speed, and other priority moves from breaking Gale Wings. Tera Flying is used for damage, allowing Sharp Beak and Life Orb sets to cleanly OHKO Amoonguss, as well as some frail neutral types such as Delphox and Hisuian Typhlosion, with Brave Bird. Tera Grass gives a resistance to Water, Electric, and an important immunity to powder attacks; this is used to bypass opposing Rage Powders and Taunt an opposing Trick Room user on turn one.
  • Jolly is usually preferred for outspeeding Adamant Dragapult, Whimsicott, and Sneasler, but Adamant is also viable to maximize damage, allowing it to OHKO Amoonguss without Terastallization on Life Orb sets.
  • The last two moveslots are open to player preference and usually mix and matched, the usual 2 are Flare Blitz and Taunt, giving it an additional STAB move and extra utility, respectively, but Will-O-Wisp and Protect are also viable; the former cripples physical threats like Dondozo, and the latter is generally useful.

movesets.name: Magic Guard
movesets.description: Despite its low Attack stat, Talonflame carves out a niche as a usable wallbreaker and potent stallbreaker. Roost keeps Talonflame healthy throughout the course of a game, allowing it to reliably act as an offensive check to threats like Ogerpon-H, Great Tusk, and Iron Moth. Bulk Up gives revenge killers like Dragonite and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon a harder time at attempting to revenge kill Talonflame while threatening to let it snowball out of control. Flare Blitz smacks Steel-types like Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Iron Treads, while Swords Dance provides greater damage potential, allowing Talonflame to threaten a 2HKO on Pecharunt and OHKO Dragonite from full HP. Taunt allows Talonflame to reliably act as a stallbreaker, preventing would-be checks like Well-Baked Body Corviknight, Unaware Scream Tail, and Deoxys-D from checking it, while Will-O-Wisp provides more utility, burning switch-ins like Garganacl, Primordial Sea Zapdos, and Archaludon. Talonflame requires support from Pokemon that can wear the opposing team down, so entry hazard setters like Great Tusk, Skarmory, and Empoleon are wonderful teammates for it. Talonflame's unimpressive bulk necessitates good teammates that can switch into revenge killers like Azelf, Barraskewda, and Hisuian Electrode; hence, the aforementioned hazard setters, Iron Moth, and Blissey all work as excellent partners for it. Talonflame also notably requires teammates such as RegenVest Swampert and Meloetta that can deal with Fire-immune Electric- and Steel-types like Well-Baked Body Gholdengo, Primordial Sea Zapdos, and Archaludon.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 4 onwards

Price Range: 8-10 points

Overview: Talonflame's exceptional Speed tier, deep utility movepool including Defog, and Flame Body make it a solid utility support on a wide range of drafts. Its Fire / Flying typing provides several key resistances, including Fairy and Fighting, and an immunity to Ground, allowing it to frustrate specific attackers even with its mediocre bulk. Fast Taunt and Will-O-Wisp can hinder and disrupt slower support Pokemon, and with Gale Wings, it can even serve as a potent revenge killer in the right matchup. Talonflame is heavily reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots and has middling bulk and offenses, meaning it relies on setup or typing to do meaningful damage or check foes.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Fast Support: Taunt and Will-O-Wisp, combined with Roost and Flame Body, make Talonflame exceedingly annoying for passive foes that may rely on weak contact moves. Flame Body can give physical attackers pause, as any contact move may leave them with a debilitating burn.

Defensive Utility: Given its good defensive typing, Talonflame can invest in bulk to check specific attackers while still providing team support with Defog and U-turn. Rather than disrupting the opposing team, this variant focuses on getting teammates in safely. Flame Body also discourages weak attacks, especially U-turn, often preserving momentum.

Setup Sweeper: Bulk Up and Swords Dance can turn Talonflame into a potent late-game sweeper after its checks have been weakened or removed. Gale Wings can also provide a one-time priority attack in a pinch, and Talonflame naturally outspeeds common offensive threats like Iron Valiant and Meowscarada anyway.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Brave Bird, Flare Blitz, Acrobatics, Hurricane, Flamethrower, Overheat

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Bulk Up, Flame Charge

Utility Moves: Roost, Taunt, Will-O-Wisp, U-turn, Defog

Coverage: Steel Wing

Niche Moves

Tailwind: Talonflame can provide speed control to its teammates, including with priority in conjunction with Gale Wings.

Fire Spin: Talonflame can run a trapping set, especially in conjunction with Taunt, to punish very, very passive targets and deal chip damage to checks like Rotom-W.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: Talonflame's debilitating Stealth Rock weakness makes it fairly reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots, especially if it is also serving as the team's entry hazard control.

Niche Items

Choice Band: Choice Band takes advantage of Talonflame’s great Speed tier and powerful STAB moves to break through teams once its counters are worn down.

No Item: With Acrobatics and a desire to switch into Knock Off, no item is viable on teams with sufficient other entry hazard removal.

Sharp Beak: Sharp Beak provides a nice damage boost on setup sets without further exacerbating Brave Bird's recoil.

Tera

While Talonflame is rarely a good choice for Tera Captain, as its Fire / Flying typing is a large part of what makes it valuable, defensive Talonflame sets can use Tera to remove their Stealth Rock weakness and fish for Flame Body burns more freely. Tera Steel is an all-around good defensive typing and provides a Stealth Rock resistance, while Tera Grass and Ground can be used to patch up weaknesses to Water and Electric, respectively.

Draft Strategy

Talonflame is usually a support Pokemon, allowing it to fit on a wide variety of teams. It is rarely a Pokemon to plan your draft strategy around, but it can almost always find a way to support teammates by spreading burns, blocking opposing setup, pivoting, removing entry hazards, or otherwise being a nuisance. Its ability to still revenge kill specific threats like Iron Valiant even with a utility focus is also invaluable.

Setup Sweepers: Talonflame's ability to spread burns and Taunt passive walls can easily facilitate setup sweepers like Latias and Iron Boulder with extra setup opportunities or by neutering their revenge killers.

Slow Wallbreakers: Talonflame's pivoting and utility movepool also makes it a great choice for bringing powerful wallbreakers like Great Tusk and Raging Bolt onto the field safely; in the right matchup, it can even provide Tailwind to mitigate their poor Speed.

Sturdy Walls: Talonflame's bulk is poor, and without landing a burn or leaning on its resistances, it can easily be overwhelmed by powerful neutral attacks; teammates like Rotom-W and Uxie can patch up this weakness.

Knock Off Switch-ins: Talonflame is loath to lose its Heavy-Duty Boots, making sturdy Fairy- or Fighting-types like Clefable or Great Tusk great teammates. Gliscor deserves a special shoutout, as it can freely absorb Knock Off after Toxic Orb has activated.

Checks and Counters

Knock Off: Stealth Rock utterly ruins Talonflame's already-mediocre bulk without Heavy-Duty Boots, forcing it to forgo other items and avoid Knock Off and Trick in matchups where its team cannot reliably keep Stealth Rock off the field.

Rock- and Electric-types: Rock- and Electric-types resist Talonflame's primary STAB moves and can usually OHKO back; specially attacking variants also do not fear Flame Body.

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types are generally unthreatened by any of Talonflame’s moves and can OHKO back with impunity.

Faster Foes: Faster offensive foes, including Choice Scarf users, that can hit Talonflame at least neutrally can dramatically reduce its effectiveness.
